issue.title: A way to really sync ignore patterns
issue.body:
It would be so great if we had next to .stignore an additional file called .stignore_synced so we can define ignore patterns on one machine and don't need to manually include them on all the other nodes. 

ATM, you can include an external file in the .stignore however that entry won't get synced so basically it doesn't matter if you copy&paste one line or thousand lines on all of your nodes (except for when you change the ignore patterns, of course). With around 14 nodes this becomes a time consuming and extremely unnecessary task. This has not been considered in the issues I have found here (#424, #837 and #2115 ) so this should be reconsidered. 

Having an additional ignore file that gets synced means you only have to set up the ignore patterns on one machine and even new nodes use the ignore patterns.

issue.title: Replacing a directory with a symlink or vice versa is buggy

labels.name: bug
labels.description: A problem with current functionality, as opposed to missing functionality (enhancement)

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
I found a curious behaviour when deleting directories and creating symbolic links.

Consider two machines One and Two. In One I make a directory A with a file a and a directory B with the same file a and another file b:

> ## 1
> 
>  One:~$ mkdir A B; touch A/a; cp A/a B; touch B/b; ls -R
> A:
> a
> B:
> a b

I wait until both machines are synchronized. Later I remove directory A and replace it by a symbolic link to B

> ## 2
> 
>  One:~$ rm -r A; ln -s B A; ls -R 
>   A:
>   a b
>   B:
>   a b

Synchronization fails at Two when it tries to delete A because the directory is not empty.

> ## 3
> 
> Two:~$ ls -R 
> A:
> a
> B:
> a b

To allow synchronization to complete, I remove the directory A

> ## 4
> 
> Two:~$ rm -r A; ls B
> a b

After synchronization completes A becomes a symbolic link in machine Two, as expected, but with the undesired consequence that in the process file a disappeared from directory B in both machines, whereas it was deleted from directory A in machine Two where it was not linked to directory B.

> ## 5
> 
> One:~$ ls -R
> A:
> b
> B:
> b
> 
> Two:~$ ls -R
> A:
> b
> B:
> b

If I wait after deleting A in machine One in step ##2 above, allowing synchronization to occur, and afterwards make the symbollic link, synchronization doesn't fail and I do not loose any file

> ## 2bis
> 
>  One:~$ rm -r A; sleep 120; ln -s B A; ls -R 
>   A:
>   a b
>   B:
>   a b
> ## 3bis
> 
> Two:~$ ls -R 
> A:
> a b
> B:
> a b

I am scanning my directories every minute. So it seems that syncthing gets confused when I perform the two operations, delete a directory and immediately substitute it by a symbolic link, before the first change is detected and synched.

issue.title: Allow for secure file deletion/Move files to system recycle bin if available

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
Syncthing just deletes files. In order to remove all the leftover bits, it would be necessary to wipe the free space of the disk as it is difficult to find the file and wipe it specifically, which results in large volume of unnecessary writes. A definitive enhancement would be to either:
1. Allow for an option that enables some sort of secure file deletion mechanism that's built into syncthing
2. Implement an option to just move the file out to the system recycle bin (if available as discussed [here](https://forum.syncthing.net/t/deleted-files-by-mistake-can-they-be-recovered/5638)) or a specific "Trash" folder that needs to be set on systems where this isn't available and let another program handle the deletion
